title: Microbatch correction log - heuristics and quick samples
content:
Purpose:
Quick, portable notes for ad-hoc corrections when I run the weekly microbatches. Keep this as a live scratchpad — half log, half heuristic cookbook. Not meant to be canonical, just the fast decisions I keep reusing.

Principles I keep using (short):
- Prefer consistency over perfection. If a majority of an existing microbatch used Label A for a borderline case, align the rest to A unless there's a clear error.
- Save explicit relabel rationale in the PR comment (1-2 lines). Helps later audits.
- Small corrective scripts > manual one-offs for repeated patterns. I track patterns below.

Common error patterns and quick fixes:
1) Split/merged entities in conversational snippets:
   - Problem: multi-turn examples where user names or entities get split across lines ("Dr.\nSmith" becomes two tokens).
   - Heuristic: collapse newline-only splits when the token before ends with a prefix/title and following token starts uppercase and is short.
   - Example fix command: tidy_newline_splits --pattern "Dr\.|Mr\.|Ms\." --min_following_len 2

2) System message contamination in user turn labels:
   - Problem: bots/system tags sometimes injected in the same field as user text.
   - Heuristic: if line contains substring like "system:" or "assistant:" (case-insensitive) and the rest looks evaluative, move to metadata or strip.

3) Numeric & date normalization affecting classification labels:
   - Problem: 12/5 could be month/day or day/month depending on region; labelers inconsistent.
   - Heuristic: prefer ISO-normalized date tokens in the parsed-text field; keep original in raw_text. Flag items where parse != original for review.

4) Tokenization mismatches around emojis and punctuation:
   - Problem: emojis attached to words cause NER boundary errors.
   - Heuristic: insert a space before emoji clusters when they appear adjacent to alphanumerics during pre-tokenization pass. For label mapping, treat emoji cluster as separate token type "EMOJI".

Ambiguous cases I usually handle conservatively:
- Titles vs names: if a token is exactly one title + one capitalized token and the dataset majority labels as PERSON, tag PERSON.
- Partial URLs: when domain fragments appear ("amazon"), only label ORG if there's a TLD or explicit company context nearby.

Microbatch audit checklist (fast):
- [ ] Run stats: token length distribution, NER label counts, empty-field rate
- [ ] Sample 25 random items from each label with frequency >1000
- [ ] Run fuzzy duplicate detector; mark pair groups for consolidation
- [ ] Search for frequent regex hits (dates, emails, phone-like tokens) and spot-check 50

Quick commands I run locally: (notes to self)
- python scripts/stats.py --path microbatch_2026-03-08.json
- python scripts/fuzzy_dupes.py --threshold 0.87 --out review_dupes.csv
- scripts/cleaners/emoji_spacing.sh microbatch_*.json

Representative problem samples I saved for training the small rule-set (copied & anonymized):
- "user: got it dr\nsmith will be there"  => fix: merge newline, PERSON span: "Dr. Smith"
- "I bought it on amazon yesterday"  => leave as plain text, ORG label only if tld present in same turn
- "Payment on 12/5" (dataset includes UK/US) => normalize to 2025-12-05 in parsed_date, store original as raw_date

Notes to self about relabeling strategy:
- Batch-level relabel PR should contain: sample of changed items (10), an explanation for rule, counterexamples where we left original label, and the script used.
- When >2% of a label is changed by a single rule, create a follow-up synthetic check to make sure we didn't accidentally reassign other categories.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to handle mixed-language microbatches more elegantly? For now I tag language as metadata and avoid NER rules that assume English capitalization.
- Decide whether to include emoji-type tokens as features for classification models (ask Samir).
- Draft a short page for the data handbook summarizing these quick heuristics.

Rough timeline for next cleanup sprint:
- Mar 15: run duplicates pass and emoji spacing fix
- Mar 18: run date-normalizer and open PR for review
- Mar 22: merge fixes if no major objections

Random reminders (notes-to-self style):
- Drop a note in #labeling if you change >500 items in a microbatch (people get nervous).
- Add a short entry under "scripts/README.md" documenting the flags I used.

End of microbatch scratch notes. Keep concise; copy relevant sections into the PR body when making changes.
samples: 'got it dr\nsmith will be there' => merge newline, PERSON: Dr. Smith
'Payment on 12/5' => normalize to ISO date + keep raw_date
'I bought it on amazon' => ORG only if tld present
action_items: Add emoji token type to tokenization pipeline (low-risk)
Draft microbatch heuristics short doc for data handbook
Ask Samir about emoji features by Mar 14
